{{short description|On when the kernel of the sum of the two p-degeneracy maps is Eisenstein}}

In [[mathematics]], '''Ihara's lemma''', introduced by [[Yasutaka Ihara|Ihara]]{{sfnp|Ihara|1975|loc=lemma 3.2}} and named by [[Kenneth Alan Ribet|Ribet]],{{sfnp|Ribet|1984}} states that the kernel of the sum of the two ''p''-degeneracy maps from ''J''<sub>0</sub>(''N'')&nbsp;×&nbsp;''J''<sub>0</sub>(''N'') to ''J''<sub>0</sub>(''Np'') is [[Eisenstein ideal|Eisenstein]] whenever the prime ''p'' does not divide ''N''. Here ''J''<sub>0</sub>(''N'') is the [[Jacobian variety|Jacobian]] of the compactification of the [[modular curve]] of Γ<sub>0</sub>(''N'').{{clarification needed|date=August 2026}}
